extracted.intended_audience: scientists and researchers preparing to communicate with journalists and produce press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for scientists on crafting press releases and preparing for media interactions so coverage is accurate, timely, and relevant to target audiences. Emphasizes message design, sourcing, accessibility, and working with institutional public information officers and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-point message structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a "three-point message" with clear relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAAS advises preparing a concise three-point message before engaging media so core ideas are communicated quickly and consistently during interviews and in releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: What's new stated upfront
rubrics_metrics.description: "What's new?" — Clearly state what is new, preferably at the beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and the public want to know the novel aspect immediately; press materials should answer this question early to hook coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why readers should care
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why should readers care?" — Make the relevance to the audience explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the explanation of significance to audience values and interests so readers understand the practical or societal importance of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple verifiable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer multiple verifiable sources for the claims in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters typically consult multiple sources; provide contactable experts, corroborating data, and references so journalists can verify facts quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy paramount (facts checkable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is paramount — facts must be checkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because journalists prioritize accuracy, press releases should present verifiable facts, avoid overstating results, and include citations or data access when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive but accessible language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use language that is distinctive yet accessible to non-specialist audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in a style that stands out to reporters but remains understandable to the outlet's readers; avoid unnecessary jargon and overly technical phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information officer accessible for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the institutional public information officer (PIO) is available and reachable for follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear PIO contact details in the release; journalists rely on PIOs for background, clarification, and permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher available for interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the researcher(s) available to journalists for interviews and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of the scientist supports accurate interpretation and allows reporters to ask challenging or clarifying questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline-friendly (deliver what journalists need quickly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare materials in a deadline-friendly way so journalists can get what they need quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize reporters face tight deadlines (sometimes producing more than five stories a day); supply concise summaries, pull-quotes, images, and quick access to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-appropriate (match outlet's coverage focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the release appropriate to the outlet's audience and coverage focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor framing, level of technical detail, and relevance to the specific outlet or beat to increase the chance of pickup and accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor messages to audience values and interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt messaging to the values and interests of the intended public audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing answers and framing the release, consider what the target audience cares about so the story resonates beyond specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify journalist audience demographics and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Before engaging, identify the journalist's audience demographics and concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research the reporter and outlet to understand what angles, questions, and levels of detail are most relevant for their readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate challenging questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and prepare answers to challenging or critical questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparing for tough questions helps maintain clarity and credibility during interviews and prevents surprises that could lead to miscommunication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuality and pre-planned core messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrive punctually for interviews and have core messages pre-planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being on time and having prepared messages respects journalists' schedules and helps ensure main points are communicated despite time pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build professional networks with PIOs and beat reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate relationships with institutional public information officers and beat reporters in your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing professional networks make it easier to place stories, get context on what outlets need, and learn how to present work in journalist-friendly ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from experienced scientist-communicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek training and mentorship from experienced scientist-communicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning from peers and programs (e.g., AAAS Mass Media Fellows) improves skills for interviews, messaging, and crafting journalist-ready releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage journalism to reach a wider audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Use journalism to reach audiences beyond those actively seeking information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One objective of releases is to broaden exposure for research findings to the general public, policymakers, and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build public consciousness through consistent, accurate coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to build public consciousness by promoting consistent and accurate news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-crafted, accurate releases contribute to ongoing public awareness of scientific topics over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster enthusiasm that supports research funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate discovery stories in ways that can foster public enthusiasm and support for research funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing breakthroughs and societal relevance can help cultivate public interest that, in turn, supports sustained research investment.
